notes: 2026 brackets are the inflation-indexed brackets in the DOR 2026 Missouri Withholding Tax Formula ($1,348-wide steps, 4.7% over $9,436); the same brackets apply to every filing status. Top rate stays 4.7% (no RSMo 143.011 trigger reduction applied for 2026). Amendment 5 (income-tax phase-out) was rejected by voters on Aug 4, 2026.

Missouri's standard deduction equals the federal standard deduction ($16,100 single, $32,200 joint, $24,150 HoH for 2026 per DOR withholding formula). HoH and qualifying surviving spouse get an additional $1,400 exemption (shown as HoH personalExemption).

Modeled: the deduction for federal income tax (35%, 25%, 15% or 5% of federal tax for Missouri AGI up to $25,000, $50,000, $100,000 or $125,000; none above $125,000; capped at $5,000, or $10,000 married filing jointly) and the 20% business income deduction for Schedule C income (Form MO-A line 17). Not modeled: capital gains and Social Security/pension subtractions, credits.

dor.mo.gov blocked automated access during verification; Missouri DOR documents were read from Internet Archive copies of the official dor.mo.gov URLs (2026 withholding formula captured Oct 13, 2026; 2025 MO-1040 instructions captured Feb 15, 2026).

Simplification: the calculator applies the 20% business income deduction to net profit after the deductible half of SE tax, while the MO-1040 worksheet (line 17) and RSMo 143.022 use Schedule C net profit (line 31) before that adjustment. This understates the deduction by 20% of the half-SE-tax deduction and overstates Missouri tax by roughly $40-$100 at typical freelance incomes.

seDeduction.note: Missouri starts from federal AGI, so the deductible half of SE tax is already excluded.

seHealthInsurance.note: Inherited through federal AGI (Missouri also offers a separate qualified health insurance premium subtraction for amounts not already deducted).

retirementContributions.note: SEP-IRA and solo 401(k) deductions are inherited through federal AGI.

qbi.note: The federal QBI deduction is below AGI and not allowed; Missouri instead allows its own 20% business income deduction (RSMo 143.022; Form MO-A line 17), which the calculator models.

localIncomeTax.note: Kansas City and St. Louis City levy a 1% earnings tax on residents (and on nonresidents working in the city). Most Missouri residents do not live in either city, so it is not modeled.

estimatedTax.threshold: Missouri estimated tax expected to be at least $100
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Required annual payment is the smaller of 90% of the current year's tax (66-2/3% for farmers) or 100% of the prior year's tax; no underpayment penalty if tax after withholding is less than $500 (Form MO-2210).
estimatedTax.form: Form MO-1040ES; underpayment on Form MO-2210

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $45 online / $100 paper Articles of Organization (RSMo 347.179); the Secretary of State may add a small technology fee
businessCosts.annualReportFee: None - Missouri LLCs do not file an annual report
